abstract.p: Existing video hashing techniques for large-scale video retrieval often overlook inherent audio signals, which can potentially compromise retrieval performance. Incorporating both visual and audio signals, however, complicates neural architecture design, rendering the manual crafting of joint audiovisual neural network models challenging. To address this issue, we propose AV-NAS, a method that leverages data-driven Neural Architecture Search (NAS) within a tailored audiovisual network space to automatically discover the optimal video hashing network. Our approach offers: (1) a versatile multi-level semantic architecture based on audiovisual signals, defining a mixed search space encompassing diverse network modules such as MLP, CNN, Transformer, and Mamba, as well as operations like Add, Hadamard, SiLU, LayerNorm, and Skip; (2) a differentiable relaxation of the combinatorial search problem, converting it into a unified differentiable optimization problem which we tackle through our "coarse search-pruning-finetuning" strategy. Our experiments on large-scale video datasets show that AV-NAS can discover architectures distinct from expert designs and lead to substantial performance improvements over current state-of-the-art methods including the recently emerged AVHash.
